title: Distinguish Frontend vs Backend Responsibilities
description: Categorize software architecture responsibilities into client-side browser execution vs server-side data persistence and API processing.

title: Classify Full-Stack Responsibilities
description: Distinguish between client-side responsibilities (rendering, interaction, client state) and server-side responsibilities (database queries, authentication, business APIs).

title: Differentiate HTML, CSS, and JS Roles
description: Map specific web features and file responsibilities to the correct language: HTML for document structure, CSS for presentation, and JavaScript for runtime interaction.

title: Explain Client-Side Browser Execution
description: Trace how the browser receives assets over HTTP, builds the DOM and CSSOM, and runs the JavaScript event loop to power interactive web applications.

title: Author Syntactically Valid HTML
description: Construct well-formed HTML document fragments with matching tags, proper attribute quotes, and correct semantic elements.

title: Parse HTML Element Syntax
description: Identify and dissect opening tags, closing tags, attribute names, attribute values, and child content in HTML code.

title: Construct HTML Attributes
description: Configure elements using valid attribute name-value pairs, boolean attributes, class names, IDs, and resource URLs.

title: Nest HTML Elements Structurally
description: Construct valid hierarchical DOM structures by nesting child elements cleanly inside parent container elements without overlapping boundaries.

title: Implement CSS Flexbox Layouts
description: Apply display: flex, flex-direction, justify-content, and align-items to build flexible 1-dimensional layouts.

title: Identify Main and Cross Axes
description: Determine the orientation of the main axis and cross axis based on the flex-direction property (row vs column).

title: Predict Flex Item Alignment & Distribution
description: Predict visual placement of flex items under combinations of justify-content (center, space-between, flex-start) and align-items.

title: Author CSS Flexbox Rules
description: Write clean, robust CSS rules using display: flex, justify-content, align-items, and gap to build real-world UI components.

title: Author and Invoke JavaScript Functions
description: Write parameterized functions, execute them with arguments, and return computed results to calling contexts.

title: Distinguish Return Values from Console Logging
description: Differentiate between producing a return value for caller expressions and emitting debug strings to the console via console.log.

title: Predict Call Expression Values
description: Trace function execution to predict what a function call evaluates to in variable assignments and arithmetic expressions.

title: Author Functions with Return Values
description: Write reusable JavaScript functions that calculate data, explicitly return results, and compose cleanly with callers.

title: Diagnose Multi-File Frontend Defects
description: Isolate HTML structure errors, CSS styling failures, and JavaScript runtime errors in a multi-file web project.

title: Diagnose Symptom Root Causes
description: Formulate hypotheses explaining broken visual or interactive behaviors by inspecting symptoms across HTML, CSS, and JS layers.

title: Formulate Debugging Hypotheses
description: Use console logs, error stack traces, and element inspection to locate exact lines containing syntax, selector, or null reference bugs.

title: Repair Multi-File Frontend Defects
description: Apply surgical code corrections to HTML markup, CSS stylesheet rules, and JavaScript DOM handlers to restore application functionality.

title: Diagnose Which Request Stage Failed
description: Given evidence from a failed network request, determine whether the failure occurred during DNS resolution, connection, or server processing, and explain what that implies about where the fix belongs.

title: Read Network Panel Timing Evidence
description: Interpret Network panel timing breakdowns (DNS lookup, connecting, waiting/TTFB) to identify which stage of a request consumed the time or produced the failure.

title: Explain the Request/Response Cycle
description: Explain the browser-to-server request/response cycle in plain language, correctly distinguishing a request from a response with a concrete example of each.

title: Trace the Page Load Sequence
description: Reproduce, for a new URL, the sequence from link activation through DNS lookup, HTTP request, server response, and browser rendering, with a one-sentence explanation of each stage.

title: Classify Client vs. Server Responsibility
description: Given a real feature, correctly identify which responsibilities belong primarily to the browser, which belong to the server, and which involve both — and explain why important authorization and durable data cannot rely only on the browser.

title: Use the Learn / Practice / Grow Loop
description: Identify where learning, practice, feedback, and progress tracking fit into the Forge experience, and describe what to do after completing a lesson.

title: Build Responsive Navigation & Overlay Layouts with Flexbox
description: Apply flex container/item configuration, axis alignment, and distribution together to implement real-world UI components such as a responsive navigation bar or a centered modal overlay.

title: Build a Basic HTML Document
description: Create a minimal, valid HTML document with html/head/body and a small amount of content such as a heading and a paragraph.

title: Choose Appropriate Heading Levels
description: Select heading levels that reflect a document's logical structure rather than a desired visual size, and identify/correct heading-hierarchy mistakes.

title: Resolve Relative Paths
description: Predict how a relative path will resolve from the current document's location, and distinguish relative paths from absolute URLs.

title: Diagnose a Broken Link or Missing Image
description: Given a broken link or missing image caused by an incorrect path, identify the cause and correct it.

title: Write Effective Alt Text
description: Decide whether an image is informative or decorative and write alt text (or an empty alt) accordingly.

title: Build a Semantic Table
description: Build a table using table/tr/th/td that represents genuine tabular data, and explain why tables should not be used for page layout.

title: Build a Correctly Labeled Form
description: Build a form with input controls, each correctly associated with a label via matching for/id values, appropriate input types, and a submit control.

title: Select Appropriate Semantic Elements
description: Identify appropriate uses for header, nav, main, article, section, footer, and aside, and distinguish them from a generic div.

title: Refactor Generic Markup into Semantic HTML
description: Rewrite a block of generic div-based markup into meaningful semantic HTML, and justify why the change matters for accessibility, navigation, and maintainability.

title: Plan Document Structure Before Authoring
description: Plan the semantic regions and structure of a complete HTML page from a requirements list before writing markup, choosing structures based on content meaning rather than visual appearance.

title: Audit HTML for Structural Mistakes
description: Inspect a finished HTML document for common structural, semantic, and accessibility mistakes (broken paths, missing labels, misused headings, div-only structure) without being told where to look.
